phase: Phase 9 - Time-Series Analysis & Seasonal Temperature Dynamics

temporal_range.temporal_sparsity_note: Collocated dataset consists of episodic Argo-satellite match campaigns rather than an uninterrupted daily mooring time-series.

dataset.seasonal_framework: Monsoonal Oceanographic Seasons (DJF, MAM, JJAS, ON)

surface_mixed_layer_10m.coolest_season_arabian_sea: Summer_SW_Monsoon (JJAS) (Mean ~28.1°C due to upwelling & evaporative wind latent heat loss)
surface_mixed_layer_10m.basin_contrast: Bay of Bengal maintains a warmer, more freshwater-stratified surface layer year-round relative to the saline Arabian Sea.

thermocline_dynamics_100m.physical_drivers: Intense wind-driven Ekman pumping, coastal upwelling, and mesoscale eddy downwelling induce massive vertical isotherm heave.

deep_ocean_500m.seasonal_stability: High (<0.15°C seasonal variation across all seasons)
deep_ocean_500m.basin_contrast: Arabian Sea is consistently ~1.5°C warmer at 500m due to high-salinity Red Sea Outflow Water (RSOW) and Persian Gulf Water (PGW) intermediate intrusions.

max_positive_anomaly.mechanism: Downwelling anticyclonic mesoscale eddy in the central Arabian Sea.

max_negative_anomaly.mechanism: Post-monsoon cyclonic eddy upwelling in the Bay of Bengal.

scientific_limitations: Sparsity of collocated historical profiles (75 profiles across 13 floats with multi-month gaps and no 2022 coverage) precludes fitting secular multi-decadal climate warming trends.
Float trajectories drift with intermediate currents (1000 dbar), meaning observed temporal changes combine Lagrangian spatial displacement with Eulerian temporal changes.
Discrete sampling does not capture high-frequency diurnal or synoptic storm-induced inertial oscillations.
